Class StateList

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StoryGraphCollection<State>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StoryGraphList<State>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.NumberedList<State>
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.StateList
All Implemented Interfaces:
Iterable<State>, RandomAccess
public class StateList extends NumberedList<State>
The list of states in a story graph, which assign a value to each fluent and a numeric utility values to each character. States are typically not created directly by the user; they are created when a node is created. State objects exist separately from nodes because they can sometimes be reused by nodes which have the same fluent and utility values but are not the same because they have different character beliefs.
Author:
Stephen G. Ware

    • add

      protected State add(Value[] values, double[] utilities)
      Creates a new state with a given array of fluent values and utility values. Fluent values are expected to match the ID number of the fluent--meaning the value for fluent 0 is in index 0, the value for fluent 1 is in index 1, etc. The first utility is expected to be the author's utility. The second utility value is expected to be the utility for the character with ID number 0, the third the utility value for character 1, etc.

      This method does not check whether a state with the same fluent and utility values already exists; it always adds a new state.

      This method updates the story graph's meta-data last modified timestamp.

      Parameters:
      values - an arry of fluent values
      utilities - an array of utility values
      Returns:
      a newly created state that has been added to this list
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any of the fluent values have been removed or were not created in this list's story graph

    • add

      public State add(Function<? super Fluent, ? extends Object> values, Function<? super Character, ? extends Object> utilities)
      Creates a new state from a function that maps fluents to values and characters to utility values. The function that maps characters to utility values should return the author's utility when given null as its input. If the function that maps characters to utility values ever returns null, it will be treated as Double.NaN.

      This method does not check whether a state with the same fluent and utility values already exists; it always adds a new state.

      This method updates the story graph's meta-data last modified timestamp.

      Parameters:
      values - a function that maps fluents to values
      utilities - a function that maps characters (and null for the author) to utility values
      Returns:
      a newly created state that has been added to this list
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any of the fluent values have been removed or were not created in this list's story graph
      See Also:

      public State add(Map<? super Fluent, ? extends Object> values, Map<? super Character, ? extends Object> utilities)
      Creates a new state from a map of fluents to values and characters to utility values. The map of characters to utility values should return the author's utility for the key null. If the map of characters to utility values ever returns null, it will be treated as Double.NaN.

      This method does not check whether a state with the same fluent and utility values already exists; it always adds a new state.

      This method updates the story graph's meta-data last modified timestamp.

      Parameters:
      values - a maps of fluents to values
      utilities - a map of characters (and null for the author) to utility values
      Returns:
      a newly created state that has been added to this list
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any of the fluent values have been removed or were not created in this list's story graph

    • remove

      public boolean remove(Predicate<? super State> predicate, Status status)
      Description copied from class: StoryGraphList
      Removes all elements from this collection for which the given predicate returns true. This method may modify other elements of the story graph and may run for a long time as a result. For example, when nodes are removed from a story graph, all edges incident to those nodes are also removed.

      If the graph was modified by this method, the elements in this collection and other elements of the graph will be renumbered.

      This method will also update the story graph's meta-data with the new number of elements of this type and the last modified timestamp.

      Overrides:
      remove in class StoryGraphList<State>
      Parameters:
      predicate - a predicate that specifies which elements should be removed
      status - a status object that will be updated while this method runs to reflect its current progress
      Returns:
      true if any elements were removed and the graph was modified, false if nothing was removed and the graph was not modified

    • prune

      protected boolean prune(Predicate<Object> predicate, Status status)
      For each element in this collection, this method removes any reference in that element to other elements whose ID numbers have been set to Settings.PRUNED and, if the given predicate returns true, sets the element's ID number to Settings.PRUNED to signal that it should also be removed from this graph. This method does not remove elements from this collection for which the predicate returns true; it only sets their ID numbers to signal that they should later be removed, which typically happens when the collection is renumbered.

      If the number of fluents or StoryGraph.characters in a story graph have changed since any of the states in this list were created, those states will be modified to reflect the changes.

      Overrides:
      prune in class NumberedList<State>
      Parameters:
      predicate - a predicate that specifies which elements should be removed from from a story graph
      status - a status object that will be updated while this method runs to reflect its current progress
      Returns:
      true if the predicate returned true for any elements in this collection
